item.mechanism: Second-phase strengthening via in-situ formed brittle ceramic particles (TiC and Al2O3) interacting with dislocations and acting as barriers to deformation.
item.system: NbMoCrTiAl HEA composite with 32.2 vol.% TiC and 7.0 vol.% Al2O3 particles synthesized via powder metallurgy and spark plasma sintering.
item.operating_conditions: Room temperature compression testing (strain rate 10^-3 s^-1) on samples sintered at 1700 °C for 30 min under 30 MPa pressure.
item.supporting_observation: Compressive fracture strength increased from 1010 MPa (as-cast) to 1542 MPa (composite), attributed to the introduction of brittle ceramic reinforcements.
item.scope_limits: The mechanism is specific to the in-situ formation method using stearic acid as a carbon and oxygen source; the text notes that the composite exhibits typical cleavage fracture without ductility, limiting its applicability where plasticity is required.
item.alternatives_considered: Direct addition of reinforcement particles (mentioned as a less effective alternative due to potential defects like pores and cracks).
quotes: The most important one is the effect of second phase strengthening.
Introduction of brittle ceramic reinforcements would significantly increase mechanical properties of the material.
The composite created a kind of material with highly improved compressive strength, increasing from 1010 MPa to 1542 MPa.

item.mechanism: Grain refinement strengthening where the powder metallurgy (P/M) process and hard phase distribution at grain boundaries suppress grain growth and refine the matrix.
item.system: NbMoCrTiAl HEA composite processed by high energy ball milling and spark plasma sintering (SPS).
item.operating_conditions: Sintering at 1700 °C for 30 min; room temperature mechanical testing.
item.supporting_observation: Grain size reduced from ~100 μm in the as-homogenized phase to a much lower value in the composite due to the PM process and hard phases acting as barriers.
item.scope_limits: The text states this is an effective approach compared to arc-melting but does not quantify the exact grain size of the composite, only that it is 'much lower' than 100 μm.
item.alternatives_considered: Arc-melting process which results in dendritic structures with severe composition segregation.
quotes: The grain size of the as-homogenized NbMoCrTiAl phase is about 100 μm, while that of the composite is much lower.
The hard phases evenly distributed at the grain boundary, acting as the barrier of grain growth.
The PM process is an effective approach to refine grains compared to arc-melting.

item.mechanism: Solid solution strengthening caused by interstitial atoms (C and O) creating strain fields that interact with gliding dislocations.
item.system: BCC solid solution phase within the NbMoCrTiAl composite containing 0.69 at.% O and 1.28 at.% C.
item.operating_conditions: Room temperature compression; material processed via ball milling and SPS.
item.supporting_observation: The presence of interstitial atoms with substantially smaller sizes than metal atoms produces strain fields that impede dislocation motion, contributing to the strength increase.
item.scope_limits: The text notes that while solution strengthening occurs, the specific contribution is inferred from literature on other alloys (Fe-based) rather than direct quantification in this specific composite.
item.alternatives_considered: Solution strengthening by substitutional elements (e.g., Nb in TiC) which is noted as a separate effect for the carbide lattice constant.
quotes: These interstitial atoms will produce a substantial strain field, with which gliding dislocations will interact.
The BCC phase contains 0.69 at. % O and 1.28 at. % C, which may cause significant increase in strength.
Solution-strengthening effect resulted in the improved mechanical properties.

item.mechanism: In-situ formation of TiC and Al2O3 phases via reaction sintering using stearic acid as a process control agent and source of C and O.
item.system: NbMoCrTiAl composite synthesized from elemental powders (Nb, Mo, Cr, Ti, Al) with stearic acid added.
item.operating_conditions: High energy ball milling for 39 h at 300 rpm in argon, followed by SPS at 1700 °C under 30 MPa.
item.supporting_observation: EPMA and XRD confirmed the presence of TiC and Al2O3 phases, with no apparent debonding, attributed to the in-situ reaction during sintering.
item.scope_limits: The mechanism relies on the specific use of stearic acid; the text notes Al2O3 was not detected by XRD likely due to the limit detection of 5%.
item.alternatives_considered: Direct addition of carbides and oxides, which the authors state can effectively reduce material defects like pores and cracks compared to direct addition.
quotes: The stearic acid was introduced as process control agent (PCA) to prevent cold welding as well as particle agglomeration, and also acted as additive for generating particulate reinforced HEA composite.
During the process of high energy ball-milling, PCA is used to not only prevent cold-welding, but also act as the source of the elements carbon and oxygen.
No apparent debonding between dispersed particles and the HEA matrix could be found, which suggested that the secondary phase grains and the HEA grains possessed good bonding.

item.mechanism: Formation of a BCC solid solution phase predicted by thermodynamic criteria (VEC < 6.87, Ω > 1, δ < 6.6%).
item.system: NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy matrix (non-equiatomic composition: Nb20.3 Mo31.0 Cr19.3 Ti10.7 Al16.7).
item.operating_conditions: Sintered at 1700 °C; analyzed via XRD and EPMA.
item.supporting_observation: Calculated parameters (δ = 5.6, Ω = 3.46, VEC = 4.96) for the actual phase composition align with the criteria for BCC formation, verified by XRD diffraction peaks.
item.scope_limits: The text states that 'all brittle alloys have a VEC ≥ 4.6', predicting the NbMoCrTiAl RHEA should be without ductility, which matches the observed cleavage fracture.
item.alternatives_considered: FCC phase formation, which is associated with ductile alloys having VEC ≤ 4.4.
quotes: According to the empirical rules, BCC solid solutions were generally formed in HEA systems under the following certain conditions.
δ, Ω, and VEC are calculated to be 5.4, 2.92 and 4.80 respectively, so BCC solid solution could be anticipated.

item.mechanism: Solubility of Nb in TiC carbide phase due to large negative mixing enthalpy (Hmix) and identical crystal structure.
item.system: TiC reinforcing phase within the NbMoCrTiAl composite.
item.operating_conditions: Sintering at 1700 °C; analyzed via XRD and Miedema's model calculations.
item.supporting_observation: The lattice constant of TiC (0.435 nm) is slightly larger than pure TiC (0.433 nm), attributed to the solution of large radius atoms like Nb, supported by the large negative Hmix value for Nb-C pairs.
item.scope_limits: Mo, Cr, and Al could not dissolve in the TiC due to relatively weak cohesive forces, limiting the solubility to Nb.
item.alternatives_considered: Formation of other carbides or oxides that might not share the same crystal structure or mixing enthalpy characteristics.
quotes: This certain concentration of Nb incorporated during grain growth agrees with the large solubility of solute Nb-carbide in solvent TiC mainly because of their largest negative value of Hmix and identical crystal structure.
While Mo, Cr, and Al could not dissolve in the TiC due to their relatively weak cohesive force.
The different crystal parameter may result from the solution of atoms with large radius, such as element Nb (r = 0.148 nm) in this composite.

item.mechanism: Cleavage fracture mode resulting from the brittle nature of the BCC HEA matrix and ceramic reinforcements.
item.system: NbMoCrTiAl HEA composite with 60.8% BCC phase, 32.2% TiC, and 7.0% Al2O3.
item.supporting_observation: Fracture surface analysis shows river patterns characteristic of cleavage fracture, confirming the material shows typical cleavage fracture mode without ductility.
item.scope_limits: The mechanism explains the lack of ductility; the text notes the material is brittle due to VEC ≥ 4.6.
item.alternatives_considered: Ductile fracture modes, which are absent in this specific alloy system due to its composition and phase structure.
quotes: Cleavage fracture is featured by river pattern, which could be clearly seen in Figure 5.
This means that the NbMoCrTiAl HEA composite shows typical cleavage fracture mode without ductility.
Therefore, the NbMoCrTiAl RHEA should be without ductility and it is indeed a type of brittle RHEA.

item.mechanism: Superior oxidation resistance at high temperatures due to the formation of Al- and Cr-rich oxide layers.
item.system: NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy (as-cast and composite forms).
item.operating_conditions: High temperature exposure (specifically mentioned at 1100 °C for the as-cast alloy).
item.supporting_observation: The declining oxidation rate at 1100 °C is attributed to the formation of protective Al, Cr-rich oxide layers, making the composite a promising high-temperature structural material.
item.scope_limits: The text cites this property for the as-cast alloy and infers it for the composite, but does not provide new high-temperature oxidation test data for the composite itself in this paper.
item.alternatives_considered: Traditional RHEAs which generally possess poor high temperature oxidation resistance.
quotes: In consideration of the superior oxidation resistance, the P/M NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy composite could be considered as a promising high temperature structural material.
The declining oxidation rate at 1100 °C was mainly due to the formation of Al, Cr-rich oxide layers.
In order to improve the oxidation resistance properties of the RHEAs, it was reported that the Ti, Al, Cr, and Si elements are essential for the formation of protective oxide scales.
